review.translation: [also|0] [from the birds of|1] [the sky|2] {take} [seven pairs|3,4], [male|5] [and female|6], [to keep|7] {their} [offspring|8] [alive|7] [on|9] [the surface of|10] [the|12] [whole|11] [earth|12],

analysis.evidence: גַּם introduces מֵעוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם, “of the birds of the sky,” adding birds to the animals Noah has already been instructed to take.

עוֹף is in construct with הַשָּׁמַיִם, forming “the birds of the sky.” The prefix מֵ־ is partitive. שִׁבְעָה שִׁבְעָה specifies how many to take, and זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה identifies them as male and female.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition מֵ־ (from מִן) + masculine singular construct noun used collectively.

analysis.evidence: In מֵעוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם, “of the birds of the sky,” הַשָּׁמַיִם names the sky where the birds fly.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine plural noun in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: The marked שִׁבְעָה is the first numeral in שִׁבְעָה שִׁבְעָה. The repetition means “by sevens” and specifies how the birds are to be taken. The following זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה identifies them as male and female.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The marked שִׁבְעָה is the second numeral in שִׁבְעָה שִׁבְעָה. The repetition gives the count distributive force, “by sevens,” and זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה identifies the birds as male and female.
זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה means “male and female.” The two terms identify the sexes of the birds taken aboard to preserve their offspring.

draft.change: Include the animal use alongside the human use under a single sense of נְקֵבָה.
draft.definition: A female, whether human or animal.
draft.evidence: Genesis 6:19 pairs נְקֵבָה with זָכָר for the animals entering the ark. Genesis 1:27 uses the same pair for humankind.

article.summary: נְקֵבָה designates a female. Genesis pairs it with זָכָר, ‘male,’ both for humankind at creation and for the animals entering the ark.

evidence.note: Two of each are to enter the ark. זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה specifies one male and one female.
God creates humankind זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה, ‘male and female.’

opposites.note: The male is the other member of the pair.

analysis.evidence: In Genesis 7:3, זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה ‘male and female’ describes the birds to be taken into the ark. נְקֵבָה identifies the female bird in the pair.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ ‘and’ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute noun.
analysis.sense: The female of an animal pair.

analysis.evidence: זֶרַע (“offspring”) is the direct object of לְחַיּוֹת. The purpose clause explains why both male and female birds are to be taken aboard.
analysis.morphology: Piel infinitive construct with prefixed לְ expressing purpose

analysis.evidence: The birds are taken זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה, “male and female.” The purpose phrase לְחַיּוֹת זֶרַע, “to keep offspring alive,” explains how their line will continue on the earth.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, used collectively.

analysis.evidence: In עַל פְּנֵי כָל הָאָרֶץ, “on the face of the whole earth,” עַל introduces the place where offspring are to be kept alive.

In עַל פְּנֵי כָל הָאָרֶץ, the construct form פְּנֵי takes כָל הָאָרֶץ as its complement. The phrase means “over the surface of the whole earth” and describes where the birds’ offspring are to be kept alive.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, common gender, plural construct, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כָל modifies the definite singular הָאָרֶץ in עַל פְּנֵי כָל הָאָרֶץ, “over the face of the whole earth.” It expresses the full extent of the earth.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In עַל פְּנֵי כָל הָאָרֶץ, “over the face of the whole earth,” פְּנֵי supplies the idea of surface, while כָל הָאָרֶץ gives the full extent over which the birds’ offspring are to be preserved.
analysis.morphology: Noun, common gender, singular absolute, with the definite article הָ־.
